widgets_values:
## 每一镜都不是只换camera pattern
V3为每个scene保存camera / lighting / performance / emotion。留空使用确定性安全棚拍弧线；也可填与scene_count等长的JSON对象列表。整幅画面强制恰好一名人物和一张人脸，并禁止镜像、反射、投影、屏幕、海报、肖像、重影、双重曝光、背景人物和可见道具。
nodes.title: NOTE 2 · V3单人物空间合同

widgets_values:
## accepted只表示文件和合同已落盘，不表示画质通过
首次32秒阶段门的第4镜出现巨幅重复脸，已判失败并停止第5镜。V3只能降低已知风险，不能自动证明画面正确。每镜必须检查全程单人物、身份、背景、轮廓和口型；失败后换新chain，不能续用旧accepted片段。32秒/5镜通过后才允许约90秒终验。

# How to use this workflow

Three modes. They differ in two places only: whether the renderer is bypassed,
and the `end_time` on the two `AudioCrop` nodes.

---

## A. Preview the scene plan — 1 second, no GPU

1. Select `MV Renderer Multi-Ref`, press **Ctrl+B** to bypass it
2. Run
3. Read the table on `PreviewAny`: which angle each scene got, and whether it
   is singing or posing
4. Not happy? Change `seed` on `MV Auto Director` and run again

Measured at **1.1 seconds**. This is the cheapest way to iterate on an idea —
use it instead of generating short test clips. Only when the plan looks right,
press Ctrl+B again and render for real.

## B. Render a short excerpt

1. Change `end_time` on **BOTH** `AudioCrop` nodes, e.g. `1:21` → `1:41`
2. Change `chain_id`, add a `_test` suffix
3. Run

About 6 scenes for 20 seconds at `max_scene_seconds = 3.5`.

**Change both nodes to the same range.** Change one and the two audio files end
up different lengths, and the renderer refuses with
`resolves to N frames but the MV scene plan requires M`.

Worth knowing before you bother: a short run costs **more** per scene, because
the 20 GB model reloads for every scene at ~78 seconds a time.

| | Minutes per scene |
|---|---|
| Full song, 59 scenes | **1.57** |
| 20-second excerpt | **6.93** |

A 20-second test takes ~45 minutes; the whole song takes ~100. Prefer mode A.

## C. Render the whole song

1. `start_time` `0:00`, `end_time` = song length **minus 1–2 seconds**
2. Change `chain_id`
3. Run

Interrupted? Run again with the **same** `chain_id` and it resumes at the
unfinished scene. A new `chain_id` starts over. The same `chain_id` after it
already finished re-exports the old video in about a second.

---

## chain_id

`chain_id` names the run and its output folder. It is also how resume works:

| Situation | What happens |
|---|---|
| Interrupted, re-run with the **same** id | resumes at the unfinished scene |
| Finished, re-run with the **same** id | **generates nothing**, re-exports the old video |
| New id | starts from scene 0 |

The middle row is the trap: no error. You paste a new scene description, hit
Run, it finishes instantly and hands you a file — the old one.

Tell-tale signs: the run ends in seconds, no `100%|████ 6/6` sampling bar in
the console, the GPU stays quiet.

**New look means new chain_id.**

---

## The four paste-in fields

`MV Auto Director` defaults to `preset = custom`, which reads these four, in
the order they appear on the node:

| | Field | Required |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `custom_global_prompt` | **yes** — errors out if empty |
| 2 | `custom_angles_json` | no — falls back to 51 built-in angles |
| 3 | `custom_light` | no, but worth writing |
| 4 | `custom_pose` | no — falls back to 26 built-in poses |

Lock the light to a fixed position in the world so cuts do not flicker.

Constraints the node checks for you: 500 characters per field, 21 words H3
rejects, 6 phrases it silently rewrites. Full list in the repo README.

---

## Singing and posing

The character does not have to lip-sync every vocal moment. Real music videos
let the vocal run while the picture cuts to the singer just existing.

| Field | |
|---|---|
| `pose_scenes` | `"3,7,12"` or `"3-5,9"` — force those scenes to stop lip-syncing |
| `pose_every` | every Nth scene poses; ignored when `pose_scenes` is set |

A third of the scenes is a reasonable rhythm. Good places: the intro, the
outro, a breakdown, the scene right after a chorus payoff.

The scene plan is hash-signed, so this node re-signs it after editing. That is
why `scene_plan` must route **through** `MV Auto Director` and not straight
from the planner.

---

## busy_background

Leave it on **`auto`**. The node reads your scene description, looks for crowd
words (`people`, `players`, `passers-by`, `group of`…) and excludes negations
(`nobody else present`, `deserted`).

When on, it avoids pairing expensive moves (`LOW SHUTTER`, `3D ROTATION`,
`SNORRICAM`, `ARC`) with a wide shot. Measured: the wrong pairing cost **16.7
minutes** for a single scene instead of 1.7.

Only set `on`/`off` to override it.

---

## Small traps

- After a node gains or changes a field, an older saved workflow still holds
  the old value and fails with `Value not in list`. Click that field, pick a
  value, save.
- Closing the **console window** kills the server. Closing the **browser tab**
  does not — reopen `127.0.0.1:8188` and it is still there.
- Starting ComfyUI a second time while the first is alive gives
  `Port 8188 is already in use`. Close the second window and use the first.

## Multiple references

This node replaces T8's stock renderer. The stock one accepts a single image —
`mv_lipsync_advanced.py:1649` hard-codes `{"ref_image_1": reference_image}` —
while the builder underneath (`conditioning.py:392`) accepts **9 images,
3 videos and 3 audios**. This node unlocks the rest.

It does not patch the T8 pack. It wraps `build_conditioning` for the duration
of the call and restores it afterwards, so an upstream update will not undo it.

### Connecting an image is not enough

A reference only does something if the prompt names it:

| Tag | Points to |
|---|---|
| `<Picture 1>` | `reference_image` |
| `<Picture 2>` … `<Picture 9>` | `ref_image_2…9` |
| `<Video 1..3>` · `<Audio 1..3>` | reference video / audio |

Write the tags in **`custom_global_prompt`** on `MV Auto Director`:

> the man in `<Picture 1>` wearing the jacket from `<Picture 2>`, standing in
> the place shown in `<Picture 3>`

That splits **face / outfit / location** into separate images. Naming a picture
you did not connect stops the job with a clear message instead of guessing.
Writing `Picture 2` without the angle brackets is normalised automatically.

### Three things to remember

- **The extra references are not part of the resume contract.** Changing an
  image while keeping the same `chain_id` silently reuses the old scenes. The
  node prints a fingerprint of the extra reference set in `report` — when it
  changes, change `chain_id`.
- **More images of the same person means more consistency, not more variety.**
  For variety give each image a distinct job and name it in the prompt.
- **The tags are fixed for the whole chain**, so one chain is one outfit. To
  change outfits mid-song, split the song at section boundaries: one chain and
  one image per section, then join them.

Reference video needs at least 5 frames and is truncated to the scene length,
then aligned down to `17n+5`.

# Setup — read this first

This workflow renders a **complete lip-sync music video** in one run: it splits
the song into scenes, picks a different camera angle for each, generates them,
concatenates them and muxes the original song back on top. No ffmpeg, no video
editor.

Output lands in
`output/minimax_h3_t8_long_video/<chain_id>/assembled/..._master_audio.mp4`

---

## 1. Two node packs

Clone both into `ComfyUI/custom_nodes`, then restart ComfyUI:

```
git clone https://github.com/T8mars/comfyui-minimax-h3-audio-T8
git clone https://github.com/oomsurvivor/comfyui-mv-autodirect
```

The first wraps MiniMax H3 and does the generating. The second adds the two
nodes that pick camera angles and widen the reference slots. Neither needs
extra Python packages.

---

## 2. Five model files

| File | Folder |
|---|---|
| `Minimax-h3_Singularity_ref2va_Pruned_v1.3_int8.safetensors` | `models/diffusion_models` |
| `minimax_h3_ref2v_turbo_4step_v0.1_comfyui_bf16.safetensors` | `models/loras` |
| `qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_nvfp4_awq.safetensors` | `models/text_encoders` |
| `minimax_h3_video_vae_fp16.safetensors` | `models/vae` |
| `minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32.safetensors` | `models/vae` |

Roughly 41 GB in total. The diffusion model alone stages about 20 GB of VRAM,
so a 24 GB card is comfortable and anything smaller will swap constantly.

Measured on an RTX 4090: **~1.6 minutes per scene** over a full song.

Other quantisations of the same model work — pick them in the loader nodes.
The LoRA is the official 4-step turbo distillation; do not run it at 8 steps.

---

## 3. Three input files

| | Load it into |
|---|---|
| The full mixed song | top `LoadAudio` |
| **Isolated lead vocal** | bottom `LoadAudio` |
| One clear face, front or 3/4 | `LoadImage` |

The vocal stem is not optional. It drives the mouth shapes scene by scene,
while the full mix is only added back at the very end.

Use the **lead** vocal, not a stem that still has backing vocals in it. Backing
vocals humming while the lead rests read as singing, and the character will
open their mouth in the wrong places.

Put the image in `ComfyUI/input/`. `.mp3` loads fine, no need to convert.

---

## 4. Audio alignment — the one thing that will stop the run

Both audio files must resolve to the **same sample count**. A 13 ms difference
is enough for the renderer to refuse the job with:

```
vocal_lock_audio resolves to N frames but the MV scene plan requires M
```

The two `AudioCrop` nodes handle this, provided:

- both are set to the **same** `start_time` and `end_time`
- `end_time` is at least **1 second shorter** than the shorter file

On a 2:43 song, `2:42` works and `2:43` fails — cropping past the real length
clamps each file to its own duration, and they differ.

**Changing one AudioCrop and forgetting the other is the most common mistake.**

---

## 5. First run

Start with the free preview. It costs no GPU time at all:

1. Select `MV Renderer Multi-Ref`, press **Ctrl+B** to bypass it
2. Run
3. Read the table on `PreviewAny` — which angle each scene got, and whether it
   is singing or posing
4. Not happy? Change `seed` on `MV Auto Director` and run again

That takes about **1.1 seconds**. Use it to iterate on ideas instead of
generating test clips.

When the plan looks right, press **Ctrl+B** again to re-enable the renderer,
set a fresh `chain_id`, and run.

---

## 6. chain_id — understand this before your first real run

`chain_id` names the run and its output folder. It is also how resume works:

| Situation | What happens |
|---|---|
| Run interrupted, re-run with the **same** `chain_id` | picks up at the unfinished scene |
| Already finished, re-run with the **same** `chain_id` | **generates nothing**, re-exports the old video in about a second |
| New `chain_id` | starts from scene 0 |

The middle row is the trap: it does not raise an error. You paste a new scene
description, hit Run, it finishes instantly and produces a file — the old one.

Tell-tale signs: the run ends in seconds, the console shows no `100%|████ 6/6`
sampling bar, the GPU stays quiet.

**New look means new chain_id.**

---

## 7. Writing the prompt

`MV Auto Director` defaults to `preset = custom`, which reads four fields, in
the order they appear on the node:

| | Field | Required |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `custom_global_prompt` | **yes** — the node errors out if empty |
| 2 | `custom_angles_json` | no, falls back to 51 built-in angles |
| 3 | `custom_light` | no, but worth writing |
| 4 | `custom_pose` | no, falls back to 26 built-in posing actions |

Describe **who, where, and what surrounds them** in the global prompt. Lock the
light to a fixed position in the world so cuts do not flicker.

The angle library and its constraints — 500 characters per field, 21 banned
words, 6 phrases the director silently rewrites — are documented in the
`comfyui-mv-autodirect` README.

---

## 8. Not every vocal moment has to be lip-synced

Real music videos let the vocal run while the picture cuts to the singer just
existing — walking, leaning, staring off. Two fields control that:

| Field | |
|---|---|
| `pose_scenes` | `"3,7,12"` or `"3-5,9"` — force those scenes to stop lip-syncing |
| `pose_every` | every Nth scene becomes a posing scene; ignored when `pose_scenes` is set |

A third of the scenes is a reasonable starting rhythm. Good places: the intro,
the outro, a breakdown, and the scene right after a chorus payoff.

---

## 9. Scene length and total time

| `max_scene_seconds` | Scenes in a 2:43 song | Wall time |
|---|---|---|
| 3.5 | ~59 | ~100 min |
| 6.0 | ~27 | ~60 min |

Counter-intuitively, **a long run is cheaper per scene than a short one**. The
20 GB model reloads for every scene at about 78 seconds a time, so the startup
cost amortises over more scenes: 1.57 min/scene across a full song versus 6.93
min/scene on a 20-second excerpt.

So do not "just test 20 seconds". Use the free preview in section 5, then run
at least a minute of real audio.

The angle library and its constraints — 500 characters per field, 21 banned
words, 6 phrases the director silently rewrites — are documented in the
`comfyui-mv-autodirect` README.

---

## 8. Not every vocal moment has to be lip-synced

Real music videos let the vocal run while the picture cuts to the singer just
existing — walking, leaning, staring off. Two fields control that:

| Field | |
|---|---|
| `pose_scenes` | `"3,7,12"` or `"3-5,9"` — force those scenes to stop lip-syncing |
| `pose_every` | every Nth scene becomes a posing scene; ignored when `pose_scenes` is set |

A third of the scenes is a reasonable starting rhythm. Good places: the intro,
the outro, a breakdown, and the scene right after a chorus payoff.

---

## 9. Scene length and total time

| `max_scene_seconds` | Scenes in a 2:43 song | Wall time |
|---|---|---|
| 3.5 | ~59 | ~100 min |
| 6.0 | ~27 | ~60 min |

Counter-intuitively, **a long run is cheaper per scene than a short one**. The
20 GB model reloads for every scene at about 78 seconds a time, so the startup
cost amortises over more scenes: 1.57 min/scene across a full song versus 6.93
min/scene on a 20-second excerpt.

So do not "just test 20 seconds". Use the free preview in section 5, then run
at least a minute of real audio.
